title: personal-llm-inference-mini-tracker-maya-2026
body: Quick personal tracker for LLM inference micro-experiments. Purpose: capture short-run perf/cost observations, flag promising configs to move to CI bench, and list follow-ups. Informal notes, rough numbers (not audited), measured on dev cluster (dedicated-1, p4d-like). Use as a scratchpad; will copy cleaned rows into infra bench once stable.
table_rows: 2026-02-28,exp-071,redwood-13b,int8,4,512,60,150,220,11000,0.09,batching 4 increases throughput but p99 spikes; investigate scheduling
2026-03-02,exp-082,redwood-70b,fp16,1,256,120,300,420,2600,0.45,70B heavier tail latencies; try kv cache
2026-03-02,exp-085,redwood-70b,fp16,1,256 (kv cached),40,90,150,6000,0.32,enabled KV cache reduced p99 dramatically
2026-03-03,exp-093,redwood-13b,int8,8,1024,95,260,380,9000,0.08,long seq with big batch increases memory pressure
summary: Key takeaways: int8 gives consistent cost drop (~30-40%) with comparable p50 and better p99 in many configs; batching improves throughput but can increase p99 for long sequences unless KV cache is used. KV cache is high-impact for repeated prefixes (70B case). Next steps: 1) Add automated p99 spike detector for batch mixes; 2) Re-run int4 with tuned memory allocator; 3) Promote exp-085 (70B + KV) to CI bench for 48h stability run.

notes: Measuring method: synthetic prompt set (20 prompts), average over 5 runs per config. Costs are rough based on spot price estimates + model token counts. p99 variance observed between runs; flag any run with >20% delta vs previous as flaky. Remind: these numbers live in a personal space; when ready move to shared bench sheet and notify infra team.
